lines.meet: Call me Luka. I used to captain a ferry, and now I call storms, carefully, so stand behind me if a squall comes in.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're down at the Tempest Shallows too, near the landing. I'm Luka, and I've watched you come and go in the weather.
lines.ask_home: Which coast is yours? Everybody's got one, even the inland people.
lines.ask_work: What kept you busy before all this? Tell me, we've got a long crossing.
lines.answer_home: Split, in Croatia, the son of a fisherman. My wife's family is from the island of Brač.
lines.answer_work: I captained a car ferry for fifteen years, between Split and the islands. A crew of eight, and the run in every weather.
lines.chat_food: Grilled fish at my wife's konoba on Brač, with blitva and a glass of wine. Bad grilled fish is a crime, and this world is full of criminals.
lines.chat_sleep: Sailors sleep in short pieces, with one ear on the weather. Polako, it works well enough.
lines.chat_missing: The Adriatic at dawn from the bridge, flat and silver, before the first cars came aboard.
lines.chat_here: The first storm I called nearly drowned me. That's how I knew it was mine. I call it carefully now.
lines.tease_quiet: A good crew member, {name}, never says a word on the bridge. I'd sign you on.
lines.tease_talker: You'd chat to the passengers all the way to Brač and back, {name}. They'd love you, and I'd go mad.
lines.tease_careful: Sky, then sea, then sky again, before you step outside, {name}. Good, that's a sailor's habit.
lines.tease_bold: You'd sail into a bura for the fun of it, {name}. Ajme, I've buried braver men.
lines.tease_any: You're like a good crossing, {name}, rough at the start and fine in the end.
lines.tease_back: Ha, fair wind, {name}, you caught me there.
lines.take_it_kindly: That's true, {name}, and my wife would tell you so, loudly.
lines.bristle: Leave that alone, {name}. Some things you don't joke about at sea.
lines.apologise: That was out of line, and I'm sorry. The weather's in my head, not my manners.
lines.double_down: I'll not take it back. A captain says the hard thing so the passengers don't have to.
lines.needle_quiet: If you see weather coming, say so. A crew that keeps quiet loses the boat.
lines.needle_talker: Polako, polako, slow down with the talking. I can't hear the wind.
lines.needle_careful: Wait much longer and you'll miss the tide. Some crossings you have to make while you can.
lines.needle_bold: You've no respect for the weather, and the weather doesn't forgive. I've seen it, many times.
lines.needle_any: You panic on deck, and panic spreads faster than water. Keep it inside.
lines.bite_back: I've brought a ferry home through a bura with two hundred people aboard. Lecture me about the sea when you've done that.
lines.hurt: Ajme, that one went in. I'll go and watch the sky for a while.
lines.laugh_off: Seasick passengers were ruder than that every summer for fifteen years. Polako, let's keep going.
lines.confide: {name}, I had two hundred passengers aboard that morning, and I don't know what happened to one of them. I think about them every evening.
lines.listen: I'm here, {name}, on the bridge with you. Take your time, the sea's calm.
lines.look_out: Stand behind me in there, {name}, like a squall's coming. It usually is.
lines.accept: Aye aye, {name}, your heading this time.
lines.deflect: It's a splash, {name}, nothing more, so help the others first.
lines.check_in: Steady, {name}, talk to me. Where did the wave hit you?
lines.blame: Somebody steered into the weather in there, and we all went under. You know who.
lines.thank: That was deep water, and I know deep water. Hvala, thank you for pulling me out.
lines.brush_off: Polako, it's nothing at all. Sit and get your breath back.
lines.worry: Ajme, {name}, you went down like a ship in a bura. Sit, and breathe.
lines.handed_down: That was yours, and now it's on me. I'll keep it dry and stowed properly.
lines.hand_fine: Take it, it's yours now. A captain only needs his whistle.
lines.hand_sulk: A good crew asks the captain first, and nobody did.
lines.turn_friendly: I'd have you on my crew, {name}, any weather. That's high praise from a captain.
lines.turn_friends: When I get my own boat, {name}, you're first aboard. I'll keep a place on the bridge for you.
lines.turn_grating: We don't sail well together, you and me. I'll keep to my end of the boat.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll get you through the storm, because a captain does. Don't expect a glass of wine after.
lines.make_up: Enough rough water between us, {name}. Let's start the crossing again.
lines.defend: That's not fair, and I watched it all. Leave {name} alone.
lines.friend_left: The crew's a hand short with {name} away, and I feel it.
lines.friend_back: Welcome aboard again, {name}. The weather's better with you here.
lines.common_boats: Fifteen years on the bridge of a ferry, in every weather. Anybody who's worked on the water learns to be properly afraid of it.
